FAQ
What compliance certifications does Fundraise Up hold?
Fundraise Up meets leading security, privacy, and accessibility standards, including PCI DSS Level 1 v4.0.1, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001, GDPR, PIPEDA, and WCAG 2.2 AA. Together, these standards support secure payment processing, information security management, EU and Canadian data privacy, and accessible donor experiences. Audit reports and policy documents are available in our Trust Center.
Is Fundraise Up PCI DSS compliant?
Yes — Fundraise Up maintains PCI DSS Level 1 v4.0.1 compliance, the highest level of payment-card security validation. This means Fundraise Up meets more than 300 security control requirements designed to protect transactional data. Level 1 is the most rigorous PCI DSS validation tier and typically applies to organizations with the highest payment-card transaction volumes or those classified as Level 1 by card brands.
Is Fundraise Up GDPR compliant for European donors?
Yes. Fundraise Up is GDPR compliant for donor data collection, processing, and retention across all EU member states, and also meets UK GDPR requirements. The platform handles lawful basis tracking, consent capture, donor data access requests, and right-to-erasure workflows — so nonprofits can fundraise in Europe without building separate compliance pipelines.
Does Fundraise Up support PIPEDA compliance for Canadian fundraising?
Yes. Fundraise Up is PIPEDA compliant, the Canadian privacy law that governs how organizations collect, use, and disclose personal information. Combined with our 99.99% uptime and donor data protections, this means Canadian nonprofits like Canadian Red Cross and Sandra Schmirler Foundation can fundraise with full regulatory confidence.
Is Fundraise Up’s donation form accessible (WCAG 2.2 AA)?
Yes. Fundraise Up meets WCAG 2.2 Level AA standards, the recognized benchmark for digital accessibility. This includes screen reader support, keyboard navigation, color contrast compliance, and ARIA semantic markup throughout the donor journey — helping your nonprofit meet legal accessibility requirements and reach all donors.
What does SOC 2 Type II certification mean for nonprofits?
Fundraise Up holds SOC 2 Type II certification, which validates that our security controls operate effectively over a sustained period — not just at a point in time. The certification covers security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy. Annual audits are performed by an independent third-party auditor, and reports are available from our Trust Center.
Where can our IT and legal team review Fundraise Up’s audit reports?
All certifications, policy documents, audit reports, and compliance attestations are published in the Fundraise Up Trust Center at trust.fundraiseup.com. The Trust Center is updated continuously and is the single source of truth for legal, IT, and finance teams reviewing Fundraise Up.
Does Fundraise Up handle region-specific compliance like Gift Aid and tax receipting?
Yes. Fundraise Up automatically applies region-specific compliance based on a donor’s location, including UK Gift Aid eligibility, Canadian charitable receipt formats, and country-specific donor data fields. Tax receipts are issued in formats that meet the requirements of each nonprofit’s country of operation.
What is Fundraise Up’s pricing?
Fundraise Up is free to start — no setup fees, fixed subscriptions, or long-term contracts. We invest in helping you grow, and our industry-leading fee coverage helps donors offset both Fundraise Up and payment processing costs. The result: an effective Fundraise Up cost of around 1% on average after fee coverage.
